title: Greater Manchester Police says drones are 'future of policing'

input.lead: A drone unit at Greater Manchester Police is regularly following and helping to catch criminals
input.summary: A drone unit at Greater Manchester Police is regularly following and helping to catch criminals
input.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police says drones are 'future of policing' - BBC News Image source, Greater Manchester Police Image caption, Police have been using drones to track down bike thieves across the north of Manchester By Richard Stead North West Published 50 minutes ago Drones have been described a "the future of policing" after they were used to help seize 130 illegal off-road bikes across north Manchester in the less than a year. The fleet of drones is being used by Greater Manchester Police instead of the force helicopter because drones are cheaper to use and more discreet. Insp Dan Pickavance, from GMP's North Manchester Neighbourhood Policing Team, said: "All police forces can use drones - particularly in urban areas - and it means we can safely take illegal off-road bikes off the streets. "Using drones is without doubt the future of neighbourhood policing and this is an essential game-changer for us going forward." Image caption, Dan Pickavance, a neighbourhood police inspector for North Manchester, was able to monitor the images from the drone The BBC followed a police operation in which a drone was used to recover a stolen bike that had been spotted in Boggart Hole Clough. The drone was used to follow the bike to an address in nearby Charlestown, where police officers on the ground searched the property and arrested three suspects. The operation was directed by a senior police officer in the back of a van, using live images from the drone which were relayed onto a screen. title: Oldham community garden's food supply hit by dry summer

input.lead: A community garden in Oldham has lost three quarters of plants, fruit and vegetables due to hot weather
input.summary: A community garden in Oldham has lost three quarters of plants, fruit and vegetables due to hot weather
input.evidence_text: A community garden has been forced to throw away food which was destined for the local community as a result of recent dry weather Volunteers from NorthernLily CIC, a social enterprise in Oldham , said up to three quarters of its plants, fruit and vegetables simply did not survive the hot summer, and the failed crops had to be composted "Normally we grow over a tonne of food, which equates to 12,700 meals worth, and we give that away to our community," said Victoria Holden "Unfortunately, I'm not sure we'll get to a tonne this year - and that's real fresh food that normally supports our community which is now not going to be available." "We lost a lot of plants. We had to just reduce everything down in the polytunnel to what could cope with that, sometimes, 55 degree heat," she said Holden said tropical plants like the chillies, gourds, aubergines and tomatoes had survived, but the produce was "about a quarter full to where it would normally be at this stage in the year"

title: Why police are flying drones over Manchester's railway tracks

input.lead: Police drones are being launched remotely over railway lines in Manchester as part of a scheme aimed at finding trespassers and reducing delays The aircraft are kept in weatherproof boxes at sites beside the railway and can be launched remotely by pilots based in London when an i
input.summary: Police drones are being launched remotely over railway lines in Manchester as part of a scheme aimed at finding trespassers and reducing delays The aircraft are kept in weatherproof boxes at sites beside the railway and can be launched remotely by pilots based in London when an i
input.evidence_text: Police drones are being launched remotely over railway lines in Manchester as part of a scheme aimed at finding trespassers and reducing delays The aircraft are kept in weatherproof boxes at sites beside the railway and can be launched remotely by pilots based in London when an incident is reported Since the British Transport Police (BTP) launched its first site in Leeds in April 2025, four sites have been introduced across south London, as well as sites in Leicester and Manchester The BPT said Manchester was chosen because it is a known hotspot for trespass and disruption A pilot does not need to be on or near the site before the drone can take off, and the drone can also be used proactively - to patrol areas where intelligence suggests trespassing may be taking place BTP hopes to establish further sites in the North West as it expands the programme, although no additional locations have been announced so far

input.summary: Dovestones The Dovestone residents forced to take matters into their own hands as they are abused for driving home Nearly 1,000 fines were handed out last year but that has not stopped people ignoring the rules, according to those living near Doveston People living close to Doves
input.evidence_text: Dovestones The Dovestone residents forced to take matters into their own hands as they are abused for driving home Nearly 1,000 fines were handed out last year but that has not stopped people ignoring the rules, according to those living near Doveston People living close to Dovestone Reservoir fear a ‘horrendous’ parking and traffic ‘nightmare’ could return now the area is back open to the public The area around the body of water, near Greenfield in Oldham , was closed for over a month following a devastating fire that destroyed a large area of moorland from July 11. People were ordered to stay away as emergency services and fire crews tackled the blaze The major incident was stood down on August 3 with crews at the scene for several days afterwards. On August 20, it was announced the roads and car park near the reservoir would reopen That has led to concerns among those living in the area, fearful of a major influx of visitors again, especially during periods of hot weather . More tourists has meant ‘local people tend to avoid it’ Before the fire, people said litter would pile up with ‘rubbish everywhere’, empty beer bottles would be left behind, and barbecues lit despite a ban. So many cars turn up, Sarah White said: “They were blocking the roads. You couldn’t even get through at the time.”

The new system will be brought in before Christmas From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport . The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025 The town hall’s Liberal Democrat administration said it has responded to complaints in recent weeks over how it collects bins across the borough. While understood to not be directly linked to the recent controversy over open bin lids, the latest move comes after weeks of criticis Recent controversial enforcement of a long-standing policy around collecting bins with open lids led to hundreds of people being left with uncollected bins. One resident called the situation ‘woke’, another said it was ‘petty’, and a councillor claimed some areas were being ‘pick More recently, the council was accused of flipflopping after a 'bizarre' incident was recorded on a doorbell camera, which the local authority later said was a mistake .
